question: What tariffs did the US announce on 'Liberation Day' in April 2025?
text:
On **April 2, 2025**, which President Trump called **“Liberation Day,”** the U.S. announced two tiers of new tariffs: a **10% baseline tariff** on most imported goods, effective **April 5**, and **higher “reciprocal” tariffs** for selected trading partners, scheduled to start **April 9**. The higher rates **replaced** the 10% baseline for those partners; they were not added on top of it. ([whitehouse.gov](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/04/regulating-imports-with-a-reciprocal-tariff-to-rectify-trade-practices-that-contribute-to-large-and-persistent-annual-united-states-goods-trade-deficits/?trk=public_post_comment-text&utm_source=openai))

| Trading partner | Rate announced April 2 |
|---|---:|
| Lesotho | 50% |
| Cambodia | 49% |
| Vietnam | 46% |
| China | 34% |
| Taiwan | 32% |
| India | 26% |
| South Korea | 25% |
| Japan | 24% |
| European Union | 20% |

These are selected rates from the executive order’s original schedule. **Canada and Mexico** were excluded from this tariff package and remained under separate tariff rules. Some products were also exempt, including pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, and steel and aluminum already subject to separate tariffs. ([whitehouse.gov](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/eo-14257.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The announced rates changed quickly: China’s rate was raised before the original 34% took effect, and most other higher rates were paused starting **April 10**, leaving the 10% baseline in place for most trading partners. ([usitc.gov](https://www.usitc.gov/publications/332/pub5818.pdf?utm_source=openai))
